instruction: Keyframe Retime (Halve Frame Numbers) `scene.blend` contains a mesh object `Ball` with an Action driving its `location` (x, y, z). The scene's frame range is 1..200. Task: halve the time axis of the animation. Concretely: 1. For every f-curve in `Ball`'s Action, for every keyframe point, replace the frame number with half its original value. This applies to `keyframe_point.co.x` AND to `keyframe_point.handle_left.x` and `keyframe_point.handle_right.x`. The Y values (`.co.y`, `.handle_left.y`, `.handle_right.y`) MUST stay the same. Do not add or delete keyframes. Example: a keyframe at frame 80 with value 2.5 goes to frame 40 with value 2.5; a keyframe at frame 100 goes to frame 50. 2. Set `scene.frame_end = int(original_frame_end / 2)` so the scene's end frame matches the retimed animation. `scene.frame_start` stays at 1. All original frame numbers in the init file are even integers, so halving them yields exact integer frame numbers. Save the result to `answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. A mesh object named `Ball` exists in the output with the same vertex count as the input. 2. `Ball`'s Action still exists with the same number of f-curves as the input. 3. The total number of keyframes is unchanged (none added, none deleted). 4. Every keyframe's frame number (`co.x`) equals exactly half the corresponding original keyframe's frame number. 5. Every keyframe's value (`co.y`) equals the corresponding original keyframe's value. 6. `scene.frame_end == 100` (was 200). 7. `scene.frame_start == 1` (unchanged).
